Overview

Our Story

Our small Canadian-born business was founded in 1978 and has become a global organization that now spans 120 locations across 20 countries. Our expansion has been rapid, but what matters most is the common belief that drives all 5,000 of our people to be a different type of real estate organization. We believe that the places in which we live, work and play have the power to make us happier and healthier, and we are united by a shared sense of purpose, to have a positive impact on people’s lives. In short, we are a global commercial real estate advisory firm with a simple aim: for real estate to play a leading role in creating vibrant buildings, cities and places that deliver long-lasting social value and economic impact.

Why Work for Us:

We believe that our industry is changing, and we want our business to be a melting pot of curious minds, passionate hearts and strategic intelligence. Your gender, religion and race are all highly respected, but are less important to us than your ability to step up and change the game. We provide you with a place where you can do just that, with like-minded people. Collaboration is embedded in the way we work – our people have the autonomy to collaborate on client relationships, engage teams across the business, lead operations, work collectively on projects, participate in strategy and are ultimately responsible for our growth. Our distinctive Principal-led, privately-owned model puts us in the enviable position of being able to offer every employee the opportunity to own a share of our business and inspires and allows anyone to become a Principal. This role carries voting rights, so our people have a very real say in the future direction and operation of our business. This means that we are able to attract, engage and retain the best talent from the industry.

Responsibilities

• A team player who is also able to lead with humility• An ability to challenge for the better• A strong drive for results, with an unwavering focus on the end game• The desire to adapt to anything, and demonstrate agility when things don’t go to plan• A passion for building great relationships with external and internal clients• An ability to look ahead, and to understand the commercial landscape• A talent for inspiring and energising those around you

Qualifications

Degree Suitability and RTPI accredited:

BA/BSc Urban Planning BSc Town and Country Planning BA/BSc Urban and Regional PlanningBSc City and Regional Planning BA/BSc Spatial Planning MSc Urban Planning MSc Town and Country Planning MSc Spatial Planning BA/BSc Geography Only if the relevant RTPI-accredited qualification is also held

Equal Opportunities

At Avison Young, we’ve always put people at the heart of what we do.In the last few years, we’ve increased the diversity at our board, leadership and Principal levels. Avison Young stands out for our commitment to empowering women. In addition to increasing the number of women on our board and in our leadership ranks, our internal Women’s Network of more than 500 members come together for networking and learning, and advise the business on strategies for promoting access, opportunity and inclusion in our industry.Our global DEI steering committee shapes our strategy to continue to increase industry access for underrepresented groups and accelerating initiatives led by our employee resource groups, including our Women’s Network, Black Professionals and LGBTQ+ groups. In addition to leading global initiatives, the steering committee’s work examines our policies and practices, creating accountability for results and communicating progress to our executive leadership, our clients and our communities.Our culture is underpinned by our approach to diversity, inclusion, and well-being. We are committed to building an inclusive culture that:

  • empowers all our employees to thrive,
  • reflects all backgrounds and talents,
  • allows individuals to be successful and feel a sense of belonging,
  • and foster a workplace that is supported, inclusive and has a strong sense of community between colleagues.

Avison Young is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to treating all its employees and job applicants equitably. This includes implementing deliberate strategies that advance underrepresented communities in commercial real estate careers.As a Disability Confident Employer, we are committed to removing any obstacles to inclusion. If you need any adjustments to support your application or any part of the recruitment process, such as information in alternative formats or special requirements to access our buildings, or you are eligible under the Disability Confident Scheme please contact us at and we will do everything we can to help.

We are committed to inclusion in our hiring processes, and we want to give everyone a chance to show what they can bring to our organisation. If you are not sure that you have all the skills in the person specification, please still apply. We value passion and potential in our employees, so it would be great to hear from you and why you would suit this position.Some of our roles may be remote and some roles may be specific to our offices, but you will need to confirm you have the right to work in the UK.

AlphaGov (Casa Moon LLC d/b/a AlphaGov) delivers public-sector consulting for cities, counties, school systems, special districts, utilities, and related agencies. Our work spans classification and compensation, organizational and operational studies, research and program evaluation, economic and workforce analysis, surveys and community research, and applied data and infrastructure research.

We engage experienced practitioners as project-based collaborators. Engagements are remote-first with occasional client travel. When you authorize it, AlphaGov may name you as an expert collaborator or key personnel on proposals that match your expertise. We build ready teams for live pursuits — not speculative staffing banks.

We are building a team for countywide housing plans and housing needs assessments in the Atlanta metro and the Southeast. We are looking for housing and community planners who know the Atlanta Regional Commission (ARC) planning environment and can lead engagement in Spanish and English, plus specialists in fair housing and homelessness response systems.

What you'll do

- Plan and facilitate multilingual (Spanish-English) public meetings, pop-up events, focus groups and stakeholder interviews for county and city housing plans

- Apply ARC Community Development Assistance Program (CDAP) and Asset-Based Community Development practices, and coordinate with ARC staff and community-based organizations

- Analyze fair housing conditions, such as segregation and opportunity mapping and zoning barriers, and draft equity-driven housing strategies and indicators

- Help design emergency and transitional housing frameworks and referral pathways with Continuum of Care partners

- Translate and adapt surveys and public materials and review them for plain language and cultural fit

- Draft sections of housing needs assessments, strategic housing plans and implementation matrices

Requirements

Required:

  • 5+ years in housing planning, community development, urban planning or community engagement for public agencies
  • Experience on at least one housing study, housing plan, consolidated plan or comprehensive plan
  • Professional fluency in Spanish and English (spoken and written), or a deep fair-housing or homelessness-systems specialty
  • Experience facilitating public meetings with diverse and underserved communities
  • Ability to travel occasionally to client sites in the Atlanta metro area

Nice to have:

  • Work with the Atlanta Regional Commission, Georgia DCA or an Atlanta-metro county or city
  • AICP certification
  • Experience with AFFH, Analysis of Impediments or HUD fair housing planning
  • Continuum of Care, HMIS or coordinated entry experience
  • GIS and data visualization (ArcGIS, Tableau or Power BI)

The Federal Planner-Department of Defense will join a practice of more than 40 experienced planners, GIS professionals, design associates, and project managers as the task lead and lead planner on multi-disciplinary planning projects for U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) clients. The ideal candidate will be driven, intellectually curious, and committed to excellence. This role requires strong analytical skills, real property expertise, and a minimum of 5 years of experience working with or for the DoD on federal planning projects. Please note that this role requires U.S. Citizenship and travel on-site to DoD locations in the U.S. and overseas.

Anticipated work includes:

  • Lead federal planning projects for DoD clients and facilitate successful outcomes.
  • Support project-based DoD client and stakeholder engagement both virtually and in-person.
  • Prepare deliverables, such as Master Plans, Requirements Analyses, Planning Charrette Reports, and Facility Space Plans.
  • Work with Project Managers to organize project teams to ensure deliverables are submitted on time, within scope, and to the client’s satisfaction.

The ideal candidate will possess:

  • Advanced knowledge of federal planning principles, military mission priorities, and DoD real property assets.
  • Proven success leading projects that helped DoD clients achieve their desired planning outcomes.
  • The ability to juggle multiple, concurrent priorities and manage tasks independently.
  • Experience organizing and working with multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Proven quantitative and qualitative analytical skills to effectively convey data-driven planning.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • A track record of submitting high quality deliverables reflective of DoD client goals.

Required qualifications:

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience working with or for the DoD on federal planning projects.
  • Continuous and progressive leadership experience on DoD federal planning projects.
  • Experience using DoD data systems and guidance (please note specific DoD data systems, such as real property systems of record, in your application).
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams).
  • Availability to travel to DoD sites in the U.S. and overseas (25% of time).
  • U.S. Citizenship.

Preferred qualifications:

  • A bachelor’s degree (or higher) in urban planning or a related field or equivalent professional planning experience.
  • American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) credentialing.
  • Software skills, such as Esri ArcGIS Suite, AutoCAD, and/or Adobe Suite (please specify in your application).

COMPENSATION

The range for this role is $85,619 – $112,375; this will be dependent on the experience and expertise of the incoming candidate.

THIS POSITION CAN BE REMOTE, OR HYBRID; Periodic On-site Travel to Client Sites (25%) is Required.

Welcome to Verdantas, where innovation meets sustainability, and your career finds purpose!

At Verdantas, we’re redefining environmental consulting and sustainable engineering through our use of cutting-edge modeling and digital technology and our genuine commitment to people. Our work spans high-growth sectors like water resources, resilient land use, energy transformation, and civil infrastructure.

Our commitment to excellence, across more than 90 offices, is championed by a team of over 2,000 experts, scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists, embedded in a people-focused culture, prioritizing the well-being of our employees, clients, and the communities we serve. We partner with clients to deliver smart, data-driven solutions to complex environmental and infrastructure challenges. We don’t just solve problems; we help shape a more sustainable future.

Join a people-first culture that values your well-being, empowers your growth, and amplifies your impact. At Verdantas, your career goes beyond the expected, and your work helps build a better world.

Ready to shape the future of resilient communities?

About the Role

Verdantas is seeking an experienced environmental planning professional to join our growing California team. This senior-level position requires a seasoned CEQA practitioner who can independently lead complex environmental reviews, manage multidisciplinary teams, and serve as a trusted advisor to public- and private-sector clients.


The successful candidate must have demonstrated experience preparing and managing full Environmental Impact Reports from project initiation through certification, including scoping, technical oversight, impact and alternatives analysis, public review, responses to comments, CEQA findings, and mitigation monitoring.


Key Responsibilities

•Lead the preparation and management of CEQA documents, including Initial Studies, Negative and Mitigated Negative Declarations, full EIRs, Subsequent and Supplemental EIRs, Addenda, Findings of Fact, Statements of Overriding Considerations, and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Programs.

•Manage complex environmental planning projects from initiation through completion, with responsibility for scope, schedule, budget, staffing, document quality, risk management, and client communication.

•Direct multidisciplinary teams and integrate biological, cultural, tribal cultural, air quality, greenhouse gas, noise, transportation, hydrology, land use, and other technical analyses into clear and legally defensible CEQA documents.

•Develop environmental review strategies, evaluate impacts and alternatives, formulate feasible mitigation measures, and guide clients through complex CEQA decisions and approval processes.

•Lead agency consultation, stakeholder engagement, public meetings, and hearings while coordinating with project proponents, regulatory agencies, legal counsel, technical specialists, and decision-makers.

•Support client development, proposals, project scoping, fee development, and interviews while mentoring staff and providing QA/QC review of environmental documents and technical studies.


Minimum Qualifications

•Bachelor's degree in Environmental Planning, Environmental Science, Urban Planning, Geography, Biology, or a related field.

•At least 10 years of progressively responsible environmental planning and CEQA experience, preferably in environmental consulting.

•Demonstrated ability to independently manage and prepare full EIRs, including scoping, impact analysis, alternatives, mitigation, responses to comments, findings, MMRPs, and certification support.

•Strong knowledge of the CEQA Statute and Guidelines, California environmental regulations, and the requirements for developing defensible environmental documents.

•Proven experience managing scopes, budgets, schedules, multidisciplinary teams, subconsultants, client expectations, and concurrent assignments.

•Excellent technical writing, editing, presentation, communication, and client management skills.


Preferred Qualifications

•Experience with NEPA compliance, including Environmental Assessments and Environmental Impact Statements.

•AICP certification, an advanced degree, or another relevant professional credential.

•Experience supporting infrastructure, utility, energy, water, transportation, public agency, higher education, or community development projects.

•Established California client relationships and experience supporting proposals, interviews, and business development.

•Familiarity with GIS, environmental permitting, and regulatory compliance strategies.

$135k-170k

  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Medical
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
  • 401(k) with Company Match

Pro-Housing Planning Specialist (ON-CALL Role) - Housing & Community Development

Your passion is helping communities expand housing supply by improving local land use, development review, and permitting practices. At ICF, you can put that expertise into action by joining a team supporting the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and its partners with practical, community-informed strategies to reduce unnecessary regulatory barriers to home construction.


In this role, you will provide subject matter expertise on state and local regulatory reforms, with particular emphasis on land use and permitting practices. Your work will align with HUD’s State and Local Best Practices for Home Construction and the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, translating policy and practice into actionable training content and facilitated discussions for local stakeholders. This role may additionally support work under any of HUD’s Technical Assistance initiatives, including the Thriving Communities or Community Compass Technical Assistance programs.


This position is ON-CALL (hourly, part-time with variable hours) and work remotely. Assignments are made on a demand-response basis, so hours are completely variable.


Travel within the United States is required, and authorized travel and meals and incidental expenses will be reimbursed in accordance with applicable federal per diem rates. The consultant may remain an on-call subject matter expert for future projects, if desired.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Provide subject matter expertise on local pro-housing regulatory reforms, especially land use, zoning, development review, and permitting practices that can support increased housing supply and faster home construction.
  • Serve as an expert subject matter expert at listening sessions and trainings in locations across the United States.
  • Facilitate dialogue among local attendees to help communities identify regulatory reforms that are feasible, locally appropriate, and likely to have the greatest impact.
  • Apply HUD’s State and Local Best Practices for Home Construction and relevant provisions of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act when developing recommendations, training content, and stakeholder discussions.
  • Review and help shape HUD written products on land use, zoning, development review for local government audiences.
  • Coordinate with HUD, other TA providers, and ICF team members to ensure content is accurate, practical, consistent, and ready for delivery to local audiences.

Basic Qualifications you’ll need to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in urban or regional planning, public administration, public policy, government, real estate development, housing, or a related discipline, OR a minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience.
  • Minimum of 7 years of demonstrated experience with land use, zoning, development review, building or planning approvals, permitting modernization, or related pro-housing reforms.

Additional Experience:

  • Strong knowledge of how state and local regulatory requirements affect housing supply, development costs, project feasibility, and construction timelines.
  • Demonstrated experience translating complex policy or regulatory concepts into practical guidance for local governments, practitioners, community stakeholders, or housing industry audiences.
  • Experience developing, reviewing, or delivering training presentations and facilitating discussions with diverse audiences.
  • Ability and willingness to travel to approximately two to four listening sessions across the United States, with scheduling and hours driven by project needs.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

  • Direct experience advising municipalities, counties, states, planning agencies, housing agencies, or development partners on zoning, land use, permitting, or process improvements.
  • Familiarity with HUD housing supply initiatives, HUD’s State and Local Best Practices for Home Construction, and the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act.
  • Experience delivering a standardized, client-approved presentation deck while maintaining an engaging and responsive facilitation style.
  • Experience leading listening sessions, workshops, or peer-learning discussions that help participants assess local conditions and prioritize actionable reforms.

Professional Skills:

  • Excellent verbal, interpersonal, facilitation, presentation, and written communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, including the ability to assess local regulatory conditions and identify practical reform options.
  • Ability to deliver consistent, high-quality content while adjusting examples and discussion techniques for different community contexts.
  • Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, multi-partner environment and manage variable, project-driven assignments.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Excel.

🌍 Depuis 2005, TPF Ingénierie fait partie du Groupe international TPF, présent dans 22 pays, avec 5 250 collaborateurs.

📍La Business Unit France du Groupe TPF, composée de TPF Ingénierie et de ses filiales réunit aujourd’hui plus de 500 collaborateurs répartis sur 20 implantations.

💡L’ingénierie Co-Créative est au cœur de notre approche : elle place l’ingénieur dans une dynamique collaborative dès la genèse du projet, aux côtés de tous les acteurs pour concilier innovation, qualité, délais, coûts et performance environnementale.

🌱 Engagée et responsable, notre démarche RSE a été récompensée en mai 2025 par la médaille Platine EcoVadis, nous plaçant dans le top 1 % des entreprises les mieux notées à l’échelle mondiale.

👀 Que recherchons nous ?

L’équipe que vous allez rejoindre

Une équipe dynamique qui accompagne et facilite la réalisation des projets publics comme privés dans toute la France dans le respect et la prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux.

Une équipe pluridisciplinaire notamment spécialisée dans la réalisation de dossiers réglementaires et l’assistance à Maîtrise d’Ouvrage dans le domaine de l’environnement et de l’aménagement du territoire. Nous accompagnons depuis près de 60 ans nos clients de la conception à la mise en œuvre des projets.

Quelques-uns de nos derniers projets : Le Nouvel Hôpital Trousseau à Tours, l’aménagement de la ZAC des Sables à Fréjus, la Rénovation Urbaine du quartier des Moulins à Nice, la révision du PLU de Blausasc (06) et des SCOT des communautés de communes du Pays de Fayence et du Cœur de Var (83).

Vos missions

·Participer à l’élaboration et l’évolution de PLU, PLUi, cartes communales et SCOT,

·Appréhender des enjeux du territoire, les analyser et les hiérarchiser,

·Compréhension du contexte juridique et administratif des projets et procédures,

·Participer à la conduite d’études pré-opérationnelles : aménagements urbains, foncières

· Production de cartographie et analyse / traitement de données SIG,

· Préparer les documents et supports nécessaires aux réunions de communication autour des projets (présentation aux élus, comités techniques ou de pilotage).

🎯 Le profil idéal ?

En cours d’obtention d’un diplôme d’une école d’urbanisme / aménagement vous disposez de connaissances dans le domaine des procédures d’urbanisme et d’aménagement.

-Vous avez une bonne capacité d’adaptation, d’analyse, d’organisation et avez le sens des responsabilités.

-Vous êtes doté de qualités rédactionnelles et d’une bonne maîtrise de la langue française.

-Vous savez faire preuve d’initiative et de créativité, et, appréciez le travail en équipe.

-Vous êtes curieux, dynamique et aimez les défis.

N’hésitez plus et rejoignez-nous !
